name: Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of localized hyperkeratotic plaques on pressure-bearing areas of palms and/or soles
Histopathological confirmation showing epidermal hyperplasia with compact orthokeratosis
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
No evidence of systemic or syndromic features associated with keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of localized hyperkeratotic plaques on palms/soles confirmed by histopathology; family history supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing may be considered to exclude syndromic forms.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized hyperkeratotic plaques on pressure points of palms and soles
searchTerms: thickened skin patches on palms and soles
hard skin spots on pressure areas of hands and feet
localized rough skin on palms and soles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Well-demarcated thickened skin lesions confined to focal areas of palms and soles
searchTerms: well-defined thick skin patches on hands and feet
clear borders thickened skin on palms and soles
focal thickened skin lesions on pressure points

common.symptomName: Pain or discomfort on weight-bearing areas of the soles
common.notes: Often exacerbated by walking or standing

common.symptomName: Cracking and fissuring within hyperkeratotic plaques
searchTerms: cracks and splits in thick skin plaques

common.symptomName: Callus formation at sites of repeated mechanical stress

occasional.notes: May cause local inflammation and pain

searchTerms: excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Nail dystrophy adjacent to keratoderma lesions
searchTerms: nail damage near thickened skin areas

rare.symptomName: Extension of keratoderma beyond focal areas to diffuse involvement
Associated mild hyperkeratosis on dorsal aspects of hands or feet
searchTerms: mild thickened skin on back of hands or feet
rough skin on tops of hands or feet

rare.symptomName: Painful fissures leading to functional impairment

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia with compact orthokeratosis and absence of epidermolysis
imaging: Not typically indicated; imaging may be used to exclude underlying bone abnormalities if clinically suspected
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with keratinocyte differentiation (e.g., KRT9) may be identified in familial cases
other: Clinical examination revealing sharply demarcated hyperkeratotic plaques localized to pressure points

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse involvement of entire palms and soles rather than focal plaques
Multiple small hyperkeratotic papules scattered over palms and soles
Lesions are punctate rather than large plaques
Presence of painful pustules and nail involvement
Progressive and often associated with genetic mutations distinct from focal PPK

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma beyond focal areas
Development of painful pustules or signs of secondary infection
Presence of systemic symptoms suggesting syndromic keratoderma
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Smith FJD, et al. Keratin 9 mutations in epidermolytic palmoplantar keratoderma. Nat Genet. 1995.
